tested_scope.positive_history: ordinary branch force-push/delete attempt while configured protection remains active
negative_controls: repository administrator or edit-repository-rules principal changes/deletes the policy

a universal impossibility claim over all GitHub or non-GitHub authorities

public_sources.observation: GitHub documents protected branches as available for public repositories on GitHub Free. By default a protection rule blocks force pushes and deletion of matching branches. The same documentation states the restrictions do not apply to repository administrators or roles with bypass permission by default, though they can optionally be applied to those actors.
GitHub documents a Do not allow bypassing setting and separate toggles for allowing force pushes and deletions. This hardens data-plane ref mutation while the policy itself remains configured.

GitHub documents repository rulesets as available for public repositories on GitHub Free, and states that repository administrators or custom roles with edit repository rules permission can create, edit, and delete repository rulesets.
GitHub documents that existing repository rulesets can be edited or deleted, confirming policy mutability is a distinct authority surface from the protected branch/tag data plane.

mechanism_matrix.candidate: repository ruleset with restrict updates/deletions and no bypass for ordinary writers

falsification.observation: Both repository-native mechanisms can prevent ref rollback/ref deletion while their policy state remains active, and public-repository documentation places these base mechanisms on GitHub Free. However, repository rulesets are themselves editable/deletable by repository administrators or edit-repository-rules principals; branch protection likewise has a separate policy-administration surface. Therefore a rollback or removal of policy state is outside the protected ref mutation predicate.
falsification.inference: A future-stateless worker cannot treat the continued existence of repository-native branch/ruleset policy as a monotonic anti-rollback witness when the negative-control authority includes a principal capable of reverting or deleting that policy, or a repository delete/recreate event that loses it. The mechanism changes prevention inside one authority domain but does not establish an immutable freshness authority outside that domain.
falsification.scope_guard: This is a bounded authority-domain falsification for repository-level protected branches/rulesets under explicit policy rollback or repository policy-loss controls. It does not claim that all organization/enterprise or external authorities fail.

phase1_result.new_evidence: Repository-native policy is stronger than current-ref detection for ordinary force-push/delete traces, but policy mutability remains a separate rollback surface and therefore does not close the Part83 future-stateless freshness gap.
phase1_result.minimal_unresolved_child: A Chat-accessible, zero-entitlement, zero-cost policy/freshness authority whose own state cannot be rolled back or deleted by the same repository-level authority being fenced, or an independently enforceable repository identity/policy monotonicity guarantee that survives delete/recreate and policy rollback.

zero_dependency_zero_quota_assessment.note: Public-repository protected branches and repository rulesets are documented on GitHub Free, but neither candidate is accepted because the tested policy-rollback/delete-recreate negative controls remain open.

continuation: Part85: execute exactly one bounded authority-separation leaf using official public documentation plus own clean state only. Test whether any zero-entitlement Chat-accessible organization/repository identity or policy surface can make repository-level anti-rollback policy monotonic across repository admin changes and delete/recreate/ref-name reuse. Required negatives: repository owner/admin policy deletion, repository transfer or recreation under the same logical name, and absence of paid organization/enterprise controls. If every stronger policy authority requires a paid/private entitlement or remains mutable by the same rollback principal, persist the exact minimal authority gap rather than accepting a handoff.
